# luz

> `@d00m-gui/luz` — a CSS-in-TypeScript theming library. A `LuzConfig`
> generates OKLCH palettes, semantic tokens, a classless HTML reset,
> utility classes, and visual component classes. It ships a Vite plugin
> and an Astro integration; it does not own application behavior.

This file is a reference for LLMs/agents configuring `luz` for a project:
`LuzConfig` fields, the custom properties `luz()` emits, the component/
utility class vocabulary, and design-system best practices for combining
them. It does not replace the docs site (human-oriented, with live demos);
treat this as the machine-readable index.

## Install & basic usage

```bash
bun add @d00m-gui/luz   # or npm/pnpm
```

```ts
// Astro: astro.config.mjs
import { luzAstro } from "@d00m-gui/luz/astro";
export default defineConfig({ integrations: [luzAstro({ primary: "#f28c20" })] });
```

```ts
// Any Vite-based framework (TanStack Start, React Router, SvelteKit, …): vite.config.ts
import { luzVite } from "@d00m-gui/luz/vite";
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [luzVite({ primary: "#f28c20" })] });
```

```css
/* your CSS entry (the one your app already loads) */
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/luz.css";
```

Same model as Tailwind v4: nothing is written to disk. The plugin
expands the generated CSS inside the file that imports it —
`luz.css` is the whole package (reset + component classes + this config's
theme + shadcn bridge + the utilities scanned from your source). `luzAstro`
is `luzVite` wired into Astro's Vite with `srcDir` as the scan root;
`luzVite` accepts `{ root }` as a second argument to scan a different
directory than Vite's `root`. `primary` is optional (default `#007dea`).

To compose your own bundle, import the pieces instead of `luz.css`, in
this order:

```css
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/reset.css";             /* classless HTML reset, static */
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/components/button.css"; /* one file per component, static */
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/components/card.css";
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/theme.css";             /* this config's tokens, generated */
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/bridge.css";            /* shadcn/ui token bridge, generated — only if you use shadcn */
@import "@d00m-gui/luz/utilities.css";         /* utilities scanned from your source, generated */
```

`@d00m-gui/luz/components.css` imports every component file at once.
All of luz's CSS lives in the `luz` cascade layer (`@layer luz { … }`):
any unlayered CSS of yours wins over it regardless of order or
specificity, with no setup. `layer(name)` on any of these `@import`s
nests it as `name.luz`. Inside a layer, luz's `!important` rules (the
`prefers-reduced-motion` and print ones) beat your unlayered
`!important`. The generated
entries (`theme.css`, `bridge.css`, `utilities.css`) are one-line files
holding a `@luz theme;` / `@luz bridge;` / `@luz utilities;` directive —
you can write those directives straight into your CSS as the equivalent
low-level API. Without the plugin they are unknown at-rules and do nothing.

Bundlers without Vite (Next.js, …) are not supported yet — a CLI that
emits the same CSS to a file is planned.

Without the plugin (server-side, any runtime — `luz()` is pure, no
`node:fs`):

```ts
import { luz, emitUtilitiesCSS } from "@d00m-gui/luz";
const { theme, tokens } = luz({ primary: "#f28c20", selector: ".brand" });
// theme — this config's `@property`s + `.brand { color-scheme; --tokens… }`
// Import reset.css and components.css separately when composing outside Vite.
const utilities = emitUtilitiesCSS(new Set(["p-4", "bg-primary-600"]), tokens);
```

`@d00m-gui/luz/color` exports the numeric OKLCH engine luz bakes shades
with (`parseColorToOklch`, `resolveBakedShade`, `luzPaletteSeeds`,
`clampToSrgb`, `formatOklch`, `luzHarmonyColorSeeds`, `WEIGHTS`, …), so a
client-side preview can match the emitted CSS exactly. Conversion and
measurement live there too: `srgbToOklch([r, g, b])` (channels 0–255) →
`{ l, c, h }`, `oklchToSrgb({ l, c, h })` → an sRGB-gamut-mapped
`[r, g, b]` tuple, `contrastRatio(a, b)` → the WCAG 2.1 ratio between two
seeds (21 for black on white).

## The four layers

1. **Classless** — plain semantic HTML (`h1`, `button`, `table`, `dialog`,
   `input`, …), no classes needed, styled by luz's reset.
2. **Utility classes** — a closed, Tailwind-nomenclature-compatible set
   (`p-4`, `bg-primary-600`, `text-lg`, `open:bg-primary-600`, `md:hidden`), scanned
   from your source and emitted as static CSS at build time. No arbitrary
   values, nothing shipped unused.
3. **Component classes** — `.badge`, `.alert`, `.card`, `.btn`, `.tabs`,
   `.menu`, … — CSS for appearance and state, **not behavior**. The native
   HTML controls in this repository's docs are standalone demos, not a
   constraint on consumers.
4. **Behavior in the consuming app** — implement interaction in JS/TS,
   preferably with accessible unstyled primitives such as Base UI (or
   Radix) for menus, tabs, dialogs, keyboard navigation and focus management.
   Attach luz classes to their rendered elements and drive the appropriate
   ARIA/data states from the behavior layer. Do not assume that a CSS class
   adds opening, selection, drag, shortcuts or accessibility behavior. The
   optional shadcn/UI token bridge aliases luz tokens for kit components.

## `LuzConfig` reference

Every field is optional; defaults below come from `LUZ_DEFAULT_CONFIG`.

### Color

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | `"#007dea"` | Base color for the primary palette, any CSS color. |
| `secondary` | derived via `harmony` | Base color for the secondary palette. |
| `tertiary` | derived via `harmony`, else `neutral` | Third palette; `"complementary"` harmony has no third color, so it falls back to neutral. |
| `quaternary` | derived via `harmony`, else an "ink" shade in primary's hue | Fourth palette; only `"analogous"` defines one. |
| `harmony` | `"complementary"` | `"complementary"` (180° rotation), `"analogous"` (30°/60°/90°), `"triad"` (120°/240°), `"monochrome"` (same hue, lower chroma). Picks how secondary/tertiary/quaternary derive from `primary` when not set explicitly. |
| `mode` | `"dark"` | `"light"` / `"dark"` (fixed palette) or `"auto"` (both emitted via `light-dark()`, resolved by `prefers-color-scheme`). |
| `neutral` | derived from `primary` | Explicit neutral palette seed. If set, `neutralTint` is ignored; `background`/`foreground` still override their separate tokens. |
| `neutralTint` | `0` | Fraction (0–1) of `primary`'s chroma carried into the neutral palette **when `neutral` is unset**. |
| `surfaceTint` | `0.4` | Fraction (0–1) of secondary/tertiary/quaternary's own chroma carried into their `surface-*` (muted background for `.surface-*`) — independent of `neutralTint`. |
| `schemeLightness` | unset | Target OKLCH `l` (0–1) for `scheme-primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary/neutral` — the shade `.btn`/`.badge`/`.alert` use. Instead of a fixed weight, picks whichever generated shade's real lightness is closest, harmonic across hues. Requires a parseable seed. |
| `schemeShade` | `{ neutral: 800 }` (else `500`) | Forces the exact weight for `scheme-*`, overriding `schemeLightness`. Number = all palettes, object = per-palette. |
| `schemeChroma` | `1` | Chroma multiplier on top of the `scheme-*` shade — tones down a loud saturated `-500` for `.btn`/`.badge`/`.alert`. |
| `accent` | `"primary"` | `"primary"` or `"secondary"`: sets live `--scheme-accent` to the corresponding `--scheme-*` for state accents. Override `--scheme-accent` per subtree. |
| `borderOpacity` | `0.3` | Global component-border alpha multiplier, exposed as live `--border-opacity`, overridable per subtree. Covers neutral, scheme, validation and selected borders, including `.alert`, `.soft` and `.outline` inset strokes. `0` hides borders without changing widths; `1` preserves the original color alpha. Focus rings and icon strokes are independent. |

### Typography

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `font` | `"sans-serif"` | Body font stack. |
| `font-headings` | `"sans-serif"` | Font stack for `h1`–`h6`. Separate field, no cascade from `font`. |
| `font-monospace` | `"monospace"` | Font stack for `code`/`pre`/`kbd`. |
| `font-emphasis` | `"cursive"` | Font stack for `em`/`i`. |
| `font-weight` | `400` | Base body `font-weight`. |
| `font-bold-weight` | `800` | `font-weight` for `strong`/`b`. |
| `line-height` | `"130%"` | Default body `line-height`. |
| `heading-letter-spacing` | `"-0.02em"` | `letter-spacing` on `h1`–`h6`. |
| `base` | `16` | Root font size (px) — drives every size/spacing token. |
| `power` | `"perfect-fourth"` (1.333) | Ratio for the exponential `text-*`/heading scale, or a raw number. Steps above `base` (`lg`…`3xl`, `h6`…`h1`) multiply by the full ratio; steps below (`sm`, `xs`) by its square root, so small text stays legible with steep ratios (`perfect-fourth`: `sm` ≈ 0.866rem, `xs` = 0.75rem). Named ratios: `minor-second` 1.067, `major-second` 1.125, `minor-third` 1.2, `major-third` 1.25, `perfect-fourth` 1.333, `augmented-fourth` 1.414, `perfect-fifth` 1.5, `golden` 1.618. |
| `sizeRelativeToBase` | `false` | Scale `size-unit`/type scale by `base / 16` instead of assuming 16px. |

### Scales & layout

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `sizeFluidRange` | `"fixed"` (via `preset`) | How far past viewport-min the fluid `clamp()` zone reaches, in scale rungs. Named: `fixed` 0 (no reflow, dense app UI), `tight` 0.35, `balanced` 1, `dramatic` 1.6 (marketing hero text). Or a raw number. |
| `preset` | unset | Shortcut for `sizeFluidRange`: `"app"` → `fixed`, `"content"` → `balanced`, `"landing"` → 2.4 (steeper than `dramatic`). Explicit `sizeFluidRange` overrides. |
| `spaceSteps` | `24` | Total `space-N` tokens. Linear and fixed (`N * base/64`), unlike the exponential type scale — the scale `p-`/`m-`/`gap-`/`w-`/`h-` utilities resolve against. |
| `radius` | `1` | Multiplier on the base radius unit (`base / 78` rem), or a literal CSS length used verbatim (`"8px"`, `"0"`). Drives `--border-radius` and the whole `--border-radius-N` scale. |
| `radiusSteps` | `8` | Total `border-radius-N` tokens (`N *` the radius unit). Linear, same shape as `space-N` — the scale `rounded-N` resolves against. |
| `spacing` | derived from `base` | `--spacing` override (page-level gutter). |
| `background` / `foreground` | `neutral` 900/100 or 100/900 by `mode` | Overrides for the base background/foreground tokens. |
| `transition` | `"all ease 200ms"` | Default `transition` shorthand via setup rules. |
| `box-shadow` | `"none"` | Default `box-shadow` token. |
| `density` | `1` | Multiplier on element padding (`--element-vertical`/`--element-horizontal`/`--element-gap`), the `--spacing` gutter and form-control chrome (range track/thumb, card radius). Does **not** scale `font-size-*`. Emitted as a live `--density` `calc()` factor — overridable per subtree/instance. `<1` denser, `>1` looser. |
| `depth` | `0` | Offset added to the nesting level `.card`/`.popover`/etc. elevation curve counts (1–4, capped). |
| `depthMax` | `0.125` | Max lightness offset from `background` the elevation curve approaches asymptotically. |
| `depthDecay` | `0.6` | Per-level falloff (0–1) of the elevation curve — smaller = more contrast between the first few levels. |
| `depthSign` | auto by `mode` | Forces elevation direction/magnitude. A `.elements-depth-light`/`.elements-depth-dark` class on a subtree still overrides this. |
| `contrastThreshold` | `0.6` | Lightness above which auto-contrast text (wheel `on-*`, `contrast-color()` fallback) flips from white-ish to black-ish. Live, overridable per subtree. |
| `stateHoverDelta` | `0.08` | Fraction (0–1) of `--foreground` mixed into `--current-bg` on `:hover` — darkens in light mode, lightens in dark, tints transparent `ghost`/`outline`. Emitted as `--state-hover-delta`, live, overridable per subtree. |
| `statePressedDelta` | `0.06` | Extra fraction of `--foreground` mixed on `:active`, added to `stateHoverDelta`. Emitted as `--state-pressed-delta`, live. |
| `statePressedShift` | `"0.1ch"` | `translateY` applied on `:active`. Emitted as `--state-pressed-shift`, live. Raise all three for a tactile brand, flatten them (`"0"`) for a flat one. |

### Escape hatches

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `vars` | unset | Raw custom properties, merged **last** — overrides an existing token by name, or adds a new one. The one field guaranteed to win over every internal calculation. |
| `properties` | `false` | Generate `@property` declarations for every token — required for the browser to animate/transition a custom property (angle, gradient stop, …) instead of snapping. |
| `selector` | `":root"` | Selector the theme block (`color-scheme` + every token) is emitted under. Set it to scope a theme to a container; add `.theme` to that container so it gets what `body` gets from the reset (font, background, color). Force light/dark per section with `color-scheme: light|dark` on the container. |

`luz().tokens.palettes` — `{ light?, dark? }` → `Record<paletteName,
Record<weight, { l, c, h }>>` — carries the numeric OKLCH of every baked
shade (palettes whose seed parsed: primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary/
neutral/surface-*/12 wheel hues), for swatches, diffs, or hex export.
`mode: "auto"` gives both schemes; `"light"`/`"dark"` only the active one.

Printing: `components/_print.css` ships a generic `@media print` layer —
forces `color-scheme: light` (so `mode: "auto"` prints dark-on-white),
hides overlays (`.drawer`, `.menu`, `.popover`, `.notice`, tooltips),
opens `<details>`, keeps fills on `.badge`/`.alert`/`.card`/`.btn`/`kbd`
(`print-color-adjust: exact`), drops `backdrop-filter`. A fixed
`mode: "dark"` bakes literal dark colors and cannot be flipped for print.

## Generated custom properties

Naming follows `--{name}-{step}` for color palettes and a fixed
vocabulary for semantic tokens:

- **Color scales**: `--primary-50`…`--primary-950` (11 fixed shades),
  same shape for `secondary`/`tertiary`/`quaternary` and `neutral`.
  Each accent palette also gets an `on-{name}` auto-contrast text color
  for its seed. Plus a 12-hue wheel, fixed names: `red`, `copper`,
  `orange`, `yellow`, `green`,
  `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `blue`, `sky`, `violet`, `pink` — each with
  its own `-50`…`-950` scale and an `on-{hue}` auto-contrast text color.
- **Scheme tokens** — `--scheme-primary`/`-secondary`/`-tertiary`/
  `-quaternary`/`-neutral` (and `-danger`/`-success`/`-warning`/`-info`):
  the shade component classes actually paint with, picked by
  `schemeShade`/`schemeLightness`, chroma-scaled by `schemeChroma`.
- **Surface tokens** — `--surface-{accent}`: a muted background per
  non-primary palette, tinted by `surfaceTint`, feeding `.surface-*`
  utility classes.
- **Anchor tokens** — `--anchor-{secondary,tertiary,quaternary,danger,
  success,warning,info,contrast}`: fixed-weight (500), chroma scaled by
  a fixed `0.6` (independent of `schemeChroma`) — used where a color
  needs to read as a link/accent rather than a scheme fill.
- **Auto-contrast** — `on-{color}` pattern (`on-scheme`, `on-btn`,
  `on-{wheel-hue}`, …): near-black or near-white text for a background,
  computed live from `--contrast-threshold`. `--on-selection` and
  `--on-badge` can be set with `vars`; without them, their CSS consumers
  derive local contrast from the active selection/badge color.
- **Surface & state** (public API — meant to be rewritten in a scope):
  `--current-bg` is "the background of this thing", and `_contrast.css`
  derives `--current-color` from it for every element, so setting
  `--current-bg` in a scope re-themes a surface without declaring any
  text color; `--on-scheme` wins over that derivation when the text color
  must be fixed. `--scheme` is the tint a component turns into its own
  `--current-bg` (solid on `.card`/`button`/`.stat`, 26% opacity on
  `.badge`, 12% mixed with `--background` on `.alert`) — set it on a
  container to tint everything inside. `--element-background` is the
  per-nesting-level surface color `_depth.css` computes (`:root` =
  `--background`), the token for a custom ornament that must match the
  surface holding it. `--scheme-accent` points to `--scheme-primary` or
  `--scheme-secondary`; focus outlines, selection, active tabs and default
  badges read it at the element, so a subtree override works. Optional
  `--element-active-border-color`, `--selection-bg`, `--tab-border-active`,
  `--badge-bg`, `--on-selection` and `--on-badge` override those local CSS
  fallbacks. `--state-hover-delta`/`--state-pressed-delta`/
  `--state-pressed-shift` are the `:hover`/`:active` deltas components
  apply on top of `--current-bg`.
- **Structural**: `--background`, `--foreground`, `--spacing`,
  `--density`, `--depth` (per-subtree elevation, see `depth*` fields),
  `--contrast-threshold`, `--scheme-accent`, `--border-opacity`,
  `--transition`, `--box-shadow`.
- **Type/space scale**: `--font-size-xs`…`--font-size-3xl` (exponential,
  `power`; √ratio below `base`) and `--font-size-small`…`--font-size-h1`
  (landmarks), each with a `-fluid` twin consumed by `.fluid`;
  `--space-1`…`--space-{spaceSteps}` (linear, `base/64` per step);
  `--border-radius-1`…`--border-radius-{radiusSteps}` (linear, `base/78`
  per step, `--border-radius` = `--border-radius-1`); `--size-unit`. None
  of them depend on `--density`.

`vars` can override or extend any of the above by exact name.

## Utility classes

Closed-vocabulary, Tailwind-nomenclature-compatible, scanned from your
source (`.astro`/`.html`/`.tsx`/`.jsx`/`.ts` by default) and emitted as
static CSS — no arbitrary values, no bracket syntax. Shape:
`{property}-{value}`, optionally prefixed by one or two variants.

- **Scale utilities** resolve against `space-N`: `p-`/`px-`/`py-`/`pt-`/
  `pr-`/`pb-`/`pl-`, `m-`/`mx-`/`my-`/`mt-`/`mr-`/`mb-`/`ml-`, `gap-`/
  `gap-x-`/`gap-y-`, `w-`/`h-`/`size-` (width + height), `min-h-`/`max-h-`,
  `top-`/`right-`/`bottom-`/`left-`/`inset-`; `rounded-N` resolves against
  `border-radius-N` (`radiusSteps`). Typography (`text-xs`…
  `text-3xl`) resolves against the exponential type scale; color
  utilities (`bg-`, `text-`, `border-`) against `{name}-{step}` palettes
  and semantic tokens, with an optional opacity suffix (`bg-primary/20`).
- **Layout literals**: `flex`/`inline-flex`/`grid`/`block`/`hidden`/
  `contents`, `relative`/`absolute`/`fixed`/`sticky`, `flex-row`/`flex-col`/
  `flex-wrap`, `items-*`/`justify-*`, `grow`/`shrink-0`/`flex-1`,
  `w-full`/`w-fit`/`w-auto`/`w-screen`, `h-full`/`h-fit`/`h-auto`/`h-screen`,
  `min-w-0`/`max-w-full`/`min-h-screen`/`max-h-full`, `inset-0`, `p-0`/`m-0`/`gap-0`, `col-span-full`,
  `aspect-square`/`aspect-video`, `rounded`/`rounded-none`/`rounded-full`,
  `overflow-*`, `truncate` (`overflow: hidden` + ellipsis + `nowrap` +
  `min-width: 0`, one class), `whitespace-nowrap`, `select-none`,
  `pointer-events-*`, `z-0`/`z-10`/`z-20`/`z-50`, `font-*`, `underline`,
  `sr-only`.
- **State variants**: `hover:`, `focus:` (pseudo-classes), `open:`/
  `closed:`/`checked:`/`disabled:`/`expanded:`/`selected:`/… (Base UI/
  Radix `data-*` states), and the arbitrary `data-[state=on]:`/
  `aria-[expanded=true]:` syntax, parsed generically — component source
  copied from Radix-/Base UI-based kits matches without luz needing to
  know the library.
- **Breakpoint variants**: `sm:`/`md:`/`lg:`/`xl:`/`2xl:` wrap the rule in
  `@media (min-width: 40|48|64|80|96rem)`; `max-sm:`…`max-2xl:` in
  `@media (max-width: calc(Nrem - 0.02rem))`. Media rules are emitted
  after the plain ones, ascending, `min-*` before `max-*`, so `hidden
  md:flex` and `flex max-md:hidden` resolve without specificity fights.
  One state variant may follow, only in `breakpoint:state:util` order
  (`md:hover:flex`, `max-lg:open:hidden`); `hover:md:flex` emits nothing.
  Values are the fixed `DEFAULT_BREAKPOINTS`; `LuzConfig` does not
  customize them.

## Component classes (curated set)

Pure CSS for appearance; behavior belongs to the consuming app. One
canonical class per component; see `covers` below for every class name
that component family also styles.

| Component | Category | Classes |
|---|---|---|
| Alert | Overlays | `.alert` — a direct-child `button` drops the alert's `--scheme` (default button look) |
| Avatar | Identity | `.avatar` (`.sm`/`.lg`), `.avatar-group` (overlapping, outlined), `.avatar.more` (overflow count) |
| Badge | Data | `.badge` — default is soft (16% tint of `--scheme`, or `--scheme-accent` without a scheme class); text mixes the scheme with `--foreground` so it reads in light and dark. Variants `.solid` (filled, auto-contrast text, `--on-badge` overrides), `.outline` (border only), `.ghost` (transparent, no border); sizes `.sm`/`.lg`; `.pill`. `justify-content: safe center`: centered while it fits, aligned to the start once the label overflows. `text-overflow` cannot reach a flex container's anonymous text: wrap the label in a child (`<span class="truncate">`) for the ellipsis |
| Blockquote | Primitives | `blockquote` — knob `--blockquote-font-size` (default `--font-size-h5`) |
| Breadcrumbs | Navigation | `.breadcrumbs` |
| Button | Primitives | `.btn`, `.button`, `.icon`, `.cta`; flat (no shadows); `.soft`/`.outline`/`.ghost` combine with any scheme class; sizes `.sm`/`.lg`; `data-role="secondary\|tertiary\|apply\|cancel\|contrast"` equals `role=` |
| Card | Surfaces | `.card` (does **not** clip: a decoration may straddle its border; a direct-child `table` opts the card into `overflow: hidden`), `.card-content` (direction under `:where()`, utilities override it), `.card-meta`, `.card-footer`, `.card-toolbar`, `.card-cover` (knob `--ratio`, default `3 / 1`), `.space`, `.card.center` — flush media (`figure`/`img`/`video`/`.card-cover`/`.card-meta` as first or last child) inherits the card radius. `.card.node` is the look of a node-editor card: its direct-child `.card-meta` becomes a title bar tinted 22% by the scheme set **on the bar itself** (`class="card-meta primary"` or `style="--scheme: var(--teal-500)"`, so the card body keeps its own `--current-bg`), with an accent `border-top`, `cursor: grab`, and `[data-dragging]` on the card for the lifted look; `.card-resize` is the bottom-trailing resize grip. Dragging and resizing themselves stay with the consumer (React Flow's `dragHandle`/`NodeResizer`) — luz only ships the look |
| Code | Primitives | `code`, `pre`, `samp` — surface tokens `--code-bg`/`--on-code`; `kbd + kbd` spacing |
| Collapsable | Surfaces | `.list` |
| Divider | Primitives | `hr` |
| Drawer | Overlays | `.drawer` (`popover`, `data-placement="left\|right\|bottom\|fullscreen"`) — non-modal by default: no backdrop, the rest of the page stays visible and clickable; `.drawer.modal` adds the `--modal-backdrop` veil, `.drawer-trigger`, `.drawer-icon`, `.radial-trigger` (`.fixed` = FAB at the bottom-right corner), `.radial-menu` (`.fixed`), `.radial-item` |
| Editable card | Primitives | `.card` |
| Element | Surfaces | `.element` (`.row`/`.column`/`.pair`/`.auto`/`.fixed`), `.element.wire` (dashed mockup placeholders) |
| Empty state | Feedback | `.empty`, `.empty-title` |
| Field | Primitives | `.field` (label > control > hint), `.field.row` (checkbox/switch), `.field:has(.field-affix)` (inline prefix/suffix inside the bordered control), `.field.short` (knob `--field-width`, default `--space-16`), `.field-hint`; `aria-invalid="true"` colors the hint, a disabled control dims the field (a placeholder `<option disabled>` does not) |
| File input | Primitives | native `input[type=file]` |
| Form | Primitives | `.form`, `fieldset`, `label`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `switch`, `.form-actions` (`.sticky`) |
| Blend Modes | Surfaces | `.background-blur`, `.background-conic-rainbow` (`.sharp`, knob `--fx-blur`) |
| Glass | Surfaces | `.glass` |
| Grid | Surfaces | `.grid` (`--grid-col-size-min` 25rem), `.grid.xs`/`.sm`/`.md`/`.lg` (9/12/18/32rem), `.grid.overflow` |
| Headings | Primitives | `h1`–`h6` |
| Hero | Surfaces | `.hero` (knob `--hero-min-height`), `.hero.compact`, `.hero-background` (absolute slot for `.background-*`/`img`/`video`), `.hero-overlay`, `.hero-content`, `.hero-heading`, `.hero-paragraph` |
| Hidden utility | Primitives | `.hidden` |
| Join | Primitives | `.join` |
| Kbd | Primitives | `kbd` |
| Layouts | Layout | `.shell` (knob `--shell-height`), `.shell.app` (full-height app root, no border), `.shell.responsive` (stacks under 48rem), `.shell.vertical`, `.shell-pane` (`.fixed`, knob `--shell-pane-width`; `.clip` = `overflow: clip` for canvas panes with floating layers), `.shell-body` |
| `light-dark()` | Feedback | (color-scheme helper, no class) |
| Link | Primitives | `a` |
| List | Layout | `.list`, `.list-row` (`a`/`button`/`details`/`li > .list-row`), `.list-col-grow`, `.list-col-wrap`, `.list-title`, `.horizontal`, `.responsive`, `.list.nav` (app sidebar rows), `.list.dense` (rows for tight panels), `.list.drilldown` (opt-in fullscreen `details` on mobile), `.list.filetree` — row metrics come from `--list-row-gap`/`--list-row-padding-block`/`--list-row-padding-inline` (defaults `--space-3`/`--space-3`/`--space-4`, `--density` applied), settable on any ancestor; `.list-title` and `details > summary` follow the same three |
| Loading | Feedback | `.loading` |
| Menu | Overlays | `.menu` (requires `popover`, invisible without it; button-anchored via `popoverTarget`; Concepto observed an anchored close jump in Chromium 152), `.menu.at-point` (`popover="manual"`; JS/TS sets viewport `--menu-x`/`--menu-y` and calls `showPopover()`; also useful for button menus where the anchor moves during close), `.menu-item` (`button`/`a` rows, `.danger`, `kbd` pushed right), `.menu-label` (section title), `.menu-separator` or a bare `hr` inside `.menu` (hairline); `--menu-transform-origin` sets transform origin |
| Modal | Overlays | `.modal`, `dialog` |
| Nav | Navigation | `nav` — `a`/`button` with `aria-current` gets the active tab color + underline (not `.tab`, `.list-row`, `.breadcrumbs`) |
| Lists (native) | Data | `ol` (decimal), `ul` (square), `dl` |
| Tabs Bottom | Navigation | `.bottom`, `.nav` |
| Notice | Overlays | `.notice` (fades after `--notice-duration`, default `10s`, paused on hover/focus-within; `.sticky` never fades; the CSS only hides it — call `hidePopover()` on `animationend` of `notice-dismiss`) |
| Page | Layout | `.page` (knob `--page-width` 88rem), `.page-header`, `.page-header-title`, `.page-body`, `.page-body.with-aside` (knob `--page-aside-width` 18rem), `.page-aside`, `.stack` (knob `--stack-gap`) |
| Pagination | Navigation | `.pagination` |
| Panel header | Layout | `.panel-header.top` (header), `.panel-header.bottom` (status bar: top hairline, small text) |
| Popover | Overlays | `.popover` |
| Progress | Primitives | `progress`, `.meter` (label + `code` value + full-width bar), `.progress` (fills any element's background up to `--progress` 0–1 with `--progress-fill` at 25%; for `.btn`, list rows) |
| Prose | Primitives | `.prose` (reading block, knob `--prose-width` 70ch, vertical rhythm, `ul`/`ol`/`dl` styling) |
| Range | Primitives | `input[type=range]` (`display-vertical`, `data-ticks`, knob `--range-length`) |
| Scroll | Layout | `.scroll-y` (knob `--scroll-max`), `.scrollbar-thin` |
| Sidebar | Layout | `.drawer-toggle`, `.drawer-sidebar`, `.list`, `.list-row` |
| Skeleton | Feedback | `.skeleton`, `.skeleton.text`, `.skeleton.avatar` (`.sm`/`.lg`), `.skeleton.badge` |
| Stat | Feedback | `.stat`, `.stat-value`, `.stat-label`, `.stat-delta` |
| Status | Feedback | `.status` (fills with `--scheme`: `.success`/`.warning`/`.danger`/…), `.status.pulse` |
| Table | Data | `table` |
| Tabs | Navigation | `.tabs`, `.tab` (gap between icon/text/badge), `.tab-input`; `.segmented`/`.toggle` style checked sibling labels, navigation `[aria-current="page"]`, or JS-managed `[aria-selected="true"]` |
| Swatch | Primitives | `.swatch` on button/span/color input; `--swatch-color` for its fill; `[aria-pressed="true"]` for selected and `disabled` for unavailable |
| Toolbar | Layout | `.toolbar` > `.toolbar-group` (adjacent groups get hairlines); `.toolbar-group.end` pushes a group to the end, `.toolbar.vertical` stacks groups and rotates hairlines, `.toolbar.floating` adds border/radius but leaves position to the app, `.toolbar.bottom` is a status bar (top hairline, `flex: 0 0 auto`, small text) |
| Target text | Feedback | `mark` |
| Emphasis | Primitives | `strong`, `b`, `em`, `i`, `small`, `abbr`, `p` |
| Text input | Primitives | `input`, `textarea`, `select` — control padding is `padding-block`/`padding-inline` (`--element-vertical`/`--element-horizontal`) under `:where()`, so a single consumer class overrides it without matching selector specificity. `select` reserves its arrow from `--select-arrow-inset` (default `--space-4`, the arrow's distance to the trailing edge; the reserved padding is that plus the arrow itself) and truncates with an ellipsis |
| Tooltip | Overlays | `.tooltip`, `[data-tooltip]` (`data-placement="top\|bottom\|left\|right"`; hidden tooltip is `display: none`, so it never adds scroll overflow) |
| Wizard | Navigation | `.wizard`, `.wizard-step` |

## Composing app layouts with `.shell`

Do not put every region directly in `.shell`. Its **direct children** are
panes: `.shell-pane.fixed` for a sidebar (`--shell-pane-width` controls its
flex basis) and `.shell-pane` for the main region. Panes use a column flex
layout; put a `.panel-header.top` before `.shell-body` and
`.panel-header.bottom` after it for a status bar. `.shell-body` fills
remaining space and scrolls. Adjacent **direct** shell children get a
hairline between them; `.shell.vertical` rotates the shell and its hairlines.
`.toolbar` has no own bottom border. Put a separator on its container if
needed, but avoid doubling the hairline between direct shell children.

```html
<div class="shell app">
  <nav class="shell-pane fixed" style="--shell-pane-width: 14rem">
    <div class="list nav"><a class="list-row" aria-current="page" href="/">Home</a></div>
  </nav>
  <main class="shell-pane">
    <header class="panel-header top"><span class="panel-header-title"><strong>Editor</strong></span></header>
    <div class="shell-body">Your app content</div>
    <footer class="panel-header bottom"><span class="panel-auto">Ready</span></footer>
  </main>
</div>
```

`.shell` defaults to `--shell-height: auto` (set a height for a bounded
workspace); `.shell.app` uses `height: 100%` and drops its outer border,
so give its ancestors a definite height. `.shell.responsive` stacks panes
under 48rem, while `.shell.vertical` stacks them at all widths. Complex
editors may nest shells inside a pane. Use the app's JS/TS state and
accessible behavior primitives for interactive pane toggles, menus and tabs;
the checkbox/label drawer examples on this repository's docs site are a
demo constraint, **not** the required architecture for consumers.

Knobs are component-prefixed custom properties with a fallback
(`height: var(--shell-height, auto)`): set them inline or on any
ancestor (`style="--page-width: 64rem"`). `_print.css` hides
`.shell.app > .shell-pane.fixed`, `.panel-header.top/.bottom` and
`.drawer` when printing.

Components that clip their children with `overflow: hidden` — a decoration
placed across their border is invisible *and* unhittable there, so
`elementFromPoint` on it returns the container: `.avatar`, `.hero`,
`.shell`, `.tabs.toggle`, `.element.pair`, `.card-cover`, `.notice.card`,
`.drawer-sidebar`, `.drawer[data-placement="fullscreen"]`, `dialog.modal`,
and `.card` only when it has a direct-child `table`. Override per instance
with the `overflow-visible`/`overflow-hidden` utilities.

Shared variant classes across most components: `.primary` (opt-in — the
unmodified default is neutral), `.secondary`, `.tertiary`, `.quaternary`,
`.neutral`, `.danger`/`.success`/`.warning`/`.info`, `.outline`, `.ghost`,
`.contrast`, plus size (`.sm`/`.lg`), shape (`.pill`, `.square`, `.block`)
and state (`.loading`, `disabled`) modifiers where the component supports
them.

## Design-system best practices

- **Pick `harmony` for the brand, not by default.** `"complementary"`
  (the default) is safe for a single-accent product UI. Reach for
  `"analogous"` when the brand needs a warm/cool family of related
  accents (marketing sites, editorial). `"triad"` reads playful/
  energetic — use sparingly, for consumer/entertainment products.
  `"monochrome"` is the right call when the brand color itself must
  dominate and a second hue would compete with it (single-color logos,
  strict brand guidelines).
- **Let `schemeLightness` do harmony work `schemeShade` can't.** A fixed
  `schemeShade` (e.g. `500` everywhere) can look inconsistent across
  hues with very different chroma curves — a saturated yellow's `-500`
  reads much lighter than a saturated blue's. Set `schemeLightness` to
  target a perceived lightness instead, and only fall back to
  `schemeShade` per-palette when one specific hue still needs a manual
  override.
- **Use `neutral` for a separate brand background hue.** When `neutral`
  is unset, `neutralTint: 0` gives gray and raising it carries some
  `primary` chroma into the neutral ramp. An explicit `neutral` seed
  replaces that derivation; `background`/`foreground` still override
  only their own tokens. `surfaceTint` independently mutes the other
  accent palettes' surfaces.
- **Use `preset` before hand-tuning `sizeFluidRange`.** `"app"` (no
  reflow) for dense, information-heavy UI where layout stability across
  viewport sizes matters more than typographic drama; `"content"` for
  docs/blogs; `"landing"` for marketing pages where large fluid type is
  a deliberate effect. Only drop to a raw `sizeFluidRange` number for a
  case none of the three presets fit.
- **`density`/`depth*` are per-context overrides, not just top-level
  config.** Both compile to live custom properties, so a dense data
  table or a modal that needs an extra elevation step can redeclare
  `--density`/`--depth` locally instead of forcing every page through
  one global value.
- **`schemeChroma` before per-color hacks.** If every `.btn`/`.badge`/
  `.alert` reads too loud against a muted UI, reach for `schemeChroma`
  globally before overriding individual palettes — it's the same
  mechanism `anchor-*` uses internally, exposed as a knob.
- **`vars` is the last-resort override, not the first tool.** Prefer
  expressing a design decision through the semantic `LuzConfig` field
  that produces it (harmony, tints, shades) so it stays coherent as
  other fields change; drop to `vars` only for a token no field
  controls, or a hard pin that must survive every other calculation
  (it's merged last, unconditionally).
- **Config always wins, but not everything is wired yet.** The intended
  end state for `luz.ts` is that any `vars` override always wins over
  internal computation, applied at the very end of the pipeline — see
  `SDD.md` in the luz repo for what's implemented vs. still in progress
  if you're contributing to luz itself rather than just consuming it.

## Generating a project's `DESIGN.md`

When configuring `luz` for a consuming project, produce a `DESIGN.md` in
that project documenting the *decisions*, not the mechanism (the
mechanism is this file / the luz docs site). Suggested sections:

1. **Brand seed** — the `primary` color and why (brand guideline, existing
   asset, etc.), plus `mode` and the reasoning (product UI → usually
   fixed `"dark"` or `"light"`; user-facing app with a system-theme
   expectation → `"auto"`).
2. **Palette derivation** — `harmony` chosen and why, any explicit
   `secondary`/`tertiary`/`quaternary` overrides and what each is used
   for in the product (not just "the accent color").
3. **Neutral & surface tuning** — `neutral` seed or `neutralTint`, plus
   `surfaceTint`, and the intended feel.
4. **Scheme tuning** — `schemeShade`/`schemeLightness`/`schemeChroma` if
   overridden, and which components they affect.
5. **Type & space scale** — `power`/`base`/`preset` (or `sizeFluidRange`)
   chosen for the product's density/reading-context, and `spaceSteps` if
   non-default.
6. **Structural knobs** — `density`, `depth*`, `contrastThreshold`,
   `accent`, `borderOpacity` if customized, and why.
7. **Escape hatches used** — every `vars` entry, with a one-line reason
   each (a `vars` entry with no documented reason is a smell — it
   usually means a `LuzConfig` field should have been used instead).
8. **Component/utility conventions** — any project-specific rule for
   which components to prefer, custom compositions built from the
   utility classes, and known component classes deliberately left
   unused.

Keep it short and decision-focused, like `luz`'s own `SDD.md` — a record
of *what's true now and why*, not a changelog or a todo list.

## Full docs

Human-oriented docs with live demos: the `docs/` app in the `luz`
repository (component pages under `/components/*`, config reference
under `/api/*`, plus `settings.astro` for a live theme playground).
